topic: Research: Llama 4 Local Deployment: Run Scout and Maverick on Your Own Hardware

key_points: Meta positions Llama 4 Scout and Maverick as open-weight, natively multimodal MoE models.
Scout has 17B active parameters, 16 experts, 109B total parameters, and a 10M-token context window.
Maverick has 17B active parameters, 128 experts, about 400B total parameters, and is designed for single H100 DGX-host or distributed deployment.
Meta says Scout can fit on a single H100 GPU with INT4 quantization, but long-context workloads still require careful serving architecture.
vLLM added day-zero support for Llama 4 Scout and Maverick in v0.8.3 or later.
Provides concrete serve commands for Scout and Maverick across 8xH100 and 8xH200 configurations.
Shows that 8xH100 can serve Scout at 1M context and Maverick at about 430K context, while 8xH200 can push Scout to 3.6M and Maverick to 1M.
Recommends fp8 KV cache for longer usable context and performance gains, and distributed inference for the full Scout context target.
Focuses on dynamic GGUF quantizations for local inference with llama.cpp-compatible tooling.
Reports Scout 1.78-bit GGUF at 33.8GB and Maverick 1.78-bit GGUF at 122GB.
Claims Scout 1.78-bit fits in a 24GB VRAM GPU at about 20 tokens/sec and Maverick 1.78-bit fits in 2x48GB VRAM at about 40 tokens/sec.
Important competitor because it targets consumer/workstation hardware rather than only datacenter vLLM setups.
Summarizes Hugging Face integration for transformers, TGI, tensor parallelism, automatic device mapping, and model hub access.
Explains the Scout and Maverick parameter layouts and native multimodal support.
Notes license acceptance is required before downloading weights from Hugging Face.
Highlights on-the-fly INT4 quantization for Scout and FP8 weights for Maverick.
Official model repository with usage snippets for Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, Docker Model Runner, and quantized local apps.
Requires Llama 4 license acceptance and accurate legal/organization details before access.
Lists Scout as a 109B-parameter BF16 safetensors model and exposes quantization links for llama.cpp, Ollama, and LM Studio-compatible workflows.
Useful for exact command examples and dependency versions such as transformers v4.51.0.

stats.fact: Llama 4 Scout uses 17B active parameters, 16 experts, and 109B total parameters; Llama 4 Maverick uses 17B active parameters, 128 experts, and about 400B total parameters.
Meta says Scout fits on one NVIDIA H100 GPU with INT4 quantization, while Maverick can run on a single NVIDIA H100 DGX host or distributed inference.
Scout supports an advertised 10M-token context window; Maverick is commonly documented around a 1M-token maximum context in deployment guides.
vLLM reports 8xH100 serving limits of Scout up to 1M context and Maverick up to about 430K context; 8xH200 increases those examples to Scout up to 3.6M and Maverick up to 1M.
vLLM recommends version v0.8.3 or later for Llama 4 Scout and Maverick support.
Unsloth reports Scout 1.78-bit dynamic GGUF shrinks from 113GB unquantized disk size to 33.8GB and Maverick dynamic GGUF shrinks from 422GB to 122GB.
Unsloth reports Scout 1.78-bit can fit in 24GB VRAM at roughly 20 tokens/sec, while Maverick 1.78-bit can fit in 2x48GB VRAM at roughly 40 tokens/sec.
Hugging Face lists Scout as a 109B-parameter BF16 model and shows local-app paths for vLLM, SGLang, Docker Model Runner, and quantizations for llama.cpp, Ollama, and LM Studio.

angles: Lead with a hardware decision tree: laptop/CPU testing, 24GB GPU Scout quant, dual 48GB workstation, single H100, H100/H200 node, and multi-node long-context serving.
Explain the MoE deployment trap: active parameters lower compute, but total parameters still dominate memory and disk.
Separate short-context chat from long-context retrieval/codebase analysis because KV cache can dominate VRAM before the model weights do.
Contrast three practical stacks: GGUF plus llama.cpp/Ollama/LM Studio for local experimentation, vLLM/SGLang for OpenAI-compatible GPU serving, and Transformers/TGI for Hugging Face-native workflows.
Warn that advertised context windows are not the same as practical context on consumer hardware; include realistic context targets per hardware tier.
Include a license/access checklist before commands so readers do not get blocked by Hugging Face gating or Llama 4 Community License requirements.
Show when Maverick is not a local-desktop model unless heavily quantized or split across multiple high-VRAM GPUs.
outline: H2: Quick answer: what hardware can actually run Llama 4 locally?
H2: Scout vs Maverick: parameters, experts, context, and practical use cases
H2: The hardware tiers: CPU, 24GB GPU, dual 48GB workstation, H100, H200, and multi-node
H2: Before you download: license access, disk space, drivers, CUDA, and Python versions
H2: Path 1 - Run Scout with GGUF on llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, or Open WebUI
H2: Path 2 - Serve Scout or Maverick with vLLM and an OpenAI-compatible API
H2: Path 3 - Use SGLang, Transformers, or TGI for multimodal and Hugging Face-native workflows
H2: Long-context deployment: why 10M tokens is not a single-GPU promise
H2: Performance tuning: quantization, KV cache dtype, tensor parallelism, batching, and context limits
H2: Troubleshooting common failures: gated weights, OOM, slow tokens/sec, image inputs, and context errors
H2: Recommended setups by goal: private chat, codebase analysis, document QA, multimodal apps, and production serving
H2: Final checklist for a reliable Llama 4 local deployment
